reason: The cited evidence directly supports the key premises: E1 and E3 confirm that adjusting V, Ti, Nb ratios and annealing at 1200 °C/8 h produces dual/multi-phase structures and improves ductility; E2 states that single-phase BCC RHEAs have ~1.5% room-temperature strain and that multi-phase designs balance strength and ductility. However, the predicted 26.9% ductility and 1775 MPa strength are attributed to a specific alloy (V5Ti35Cr5Nb40Mo15) in E1, but the text is truncated before confirming these exact values, introducing a minor gap.
premises: Adjusting V, Ti, Nb ratios in V-Ti-Cr-Nb-Mo alloys can produce dual-phase (BCC+HCP) or multi-phase (BCC+HCP+Laves) microstructures
Annealing at 1200 °C for 8 h coarsens/dissolves HCP phase, reduces Laves phase, and improves ductility
Multi-phase microstructures in RHEAs enhance strength-ductility synergy compared to single-phase BCC
Single-phase BCC RHEAs have limited room-temperature ductility (e.g., 1.5% compressive strain)
The specific alloy V5Ti35Cr5Nb40Mo15 annealed achieves 26.9% ductility and 1775 MPa strength
